Let’s talk about something that’s at the heart of every success story— community.
Chapter seven is called “The Strength of Community,” and it really drives home a simple truth: no one changes the world alone.
Think about the extraordinary women you know or have heard about. Behind each of them, there’s often a web of support—family, friends, mentors, and allies. People who cheer them on, offer a listening ear, and sometimes, give that gentle nudge when it’s needed most.
Picture a small town, where every week, a group of women gathers in a neighbor’s kitchen. They swap stories, share laughter, and give each other advice—helping one another navigate work, family, and all the curveballs life throws their way.
One day, when one of them decides she wants to run for local office, guess who’s right there by her side? The whole group rallies around her. They make campaign posters, organize events, and spread the word. And when she wins? It’s not just her determination that gets her across the finish line—it’s the community that believed in her every step of the way.
That’s the thing about success—it almost never happens in isolation. It’s built on the shoulders of those who lift us up.
Now, imagine a young inventor wrestling to bring her idea to life. She’s met with skepticism, and resources are tight. But then, she finds a mentor—an older engineer who sees her spark. Together, they put in long nights, tinkering and testing. When the invention finally works, it’s not just her win—it’s theirs. It’s proof that even a single encouraging voice can make all the difference.
And in another corner of the world, you’ll find a group of girls forming a soccer team. Even though people tell them sports aren’t for them, they practice in secret, using borrowed gear and makeshift uniforms. When they finally get to play their first game, the whole community shows up to watch. The girls lose, but the crowd cheers them on, bursting with pride at their courage and determination. Over time, more girls join, and the team becomes a symbol of what’s possible.
These stories show us something really important: community isn’t just about living in the same place or having the same background. It’s about sharing dreams and supporting one another.
A lot of us fall into the trap of thinking we need to do everything on our own. But here’s something to remember—asking for help isn’t a weakness. It’s actually a strength. Because when we come together, we can achieve more than we ever could alone.
